technical.summary: STZ shows short-term overbought conditions with strong recent price action (three white soldiers, hull flip, volume spike) but lacks trend confirmation from moving average crosses and Ichimoku; entry risk is elevated due to RSI9 extremes and weak ADX despite bullish technicals.

fundamental.summary: STZ shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signal, zero government contracts, no lobbying activity, minimal retail interest, and elevated earnings risk within 72 days—fundamentals lack bullish catalysts.

sentiment.summary: Extreme market fear (30/100) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but congressional activity is mixed with minor sales dominating and no clear conviction signal.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (306.7) indicates extreme market stress, and earnings in 72 days adds event risk; Consumer Staples defensive positioning offers limited offset to systemic conditions.

debate.key_bull_argument: Three white soldiers + hull flip + 15x volume spike with bullish OBV create strong short-term momentum setup in extreme fear environment (VIX crisis), offering contrarian entry near support at 212.03.
debate.key_bear_argument: RSI9 overbought at 74.78, Ichimoku below cloud, negative CMF/AO, weak ADX (23.93), inverted yield curve, earnings risk in 72 days, and price below 200-EMA/50-SMA create a dangerous setup where technicals lack confirmation and macro headwinds dominate.

decision.entry_rationale: While three white soldiers + hull flip + volume spike offer short-term momentum in extreme fear, RSI9 overbought at 74.78 combined with Ichimoku below cloud and negative CMF/AO create dangerous confirmation gaps that outweigh technicals.
decision.primary_risk: Earnings event in 72 days combined with inverted yield curve recession signals and VIX crisis levels create compounding event and macro risk; overbought RSI9 leaves minimal upside before pullback.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bear case dominance
